keyedRows: rule.generationReadModel · keyed · Every generation of a read model has one row keyed by read model name and generation number, and generation numbers increase by one per read model, starting at 1 (E-8, D9) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.generationReadModel

rule.generationExactlyOne · keyed · A generation is in exactly one of building, verifying, verified, active, retired, aborted or purged (E-8, D9) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.generationExactlyOne

rule.mostOneGeneration · keyed · At most one generation per read model is active, and at most one is in building, verifying or verified; these three states are the in-flight states (E-8, D9) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.mostOneGeneration

rule.allowedTransitionsNone · keyed · The allowed transitions are none to building by startGeneration, building to verifying by the backfill batch that ends the enumeration, verifying to verified by the verify batch that ends its pass, verified to active by switchGeneration, active to retired by the same switchGeneration, retired to verifying by rollbackGeneration for a generation without pauseRequired, building, verifying or verified to aborted by abortGeneration, and retired or aborted to purged by the purge batch that ends its pass; no other transition exists, and none leads from nothing to active; interruptGeneration and resumeGeneration change no state, and resumeGeneration continues the pass the progress row names, a started purge of a retired or aborted generation included, at the batch size the progress row holds, since it takes no batch size (E-8, D9, E-40) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.allowedTransitionsNone

rule.operatorEntrySpec · keyed · An operator entry of spec:application.rebuild makes the transitions named after it, a scheduled batch makes the other three, and nothing else writes a generation row (E-8, E-48, D19) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.operatorEntrySpec

rule.startGenerationRefuses · keyed · [extension] startGeneration refuses, and so makes no transition, while the tenant list of spec:command.actor-and-scope holds no row and the grants table holds one, with a message that names fillTenants, and while the tenant fill of spec:application.rebuild is in its pass fill, because a generation that walked an empty or half-filled list on a deployment whose grants predate the list would be verified and switched without the rows of the tenants it missed (E-49, E-8, Law 11) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.startGenerationRefuses

rule.readModelFirst · keyed · [extension] A read model's first generation is generation 1 in building, started by startGeneration like any other, and the read model has an active generation only after that generation is verified and switched; on a deployment with no subject the build is one backfill batch and one verify batch for each tenant of the tenant list, and one of each when the list is empty (E-8, D9) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.readModelFirst

rule.commandMaintainsRead · keyed · A command that maintains a read model writes the active generation and the in-flight generation if one exists; a retired generation is kept unchanged until it is purged and never written, and a rollback reopens it as verifying so that live commands write it again while its verify pass repairs it; a generation with pauseRequired is never reopened, because nothing would close its sources while live commands fold onto rows that missed the events since its retirement (D9, E-8) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.commandMaintainsRead

rule.generationWrittenProjection · keyed · [extension] Each generation is written with the projection whose version its row records, on the live path and by its batches alike, so the rows of one generation are one truth of one projection version (E-9, E-8, D8) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.generationWrittenProjection

rule.queryReadsActive · keyed · A query reads the active generation and nothing else; a query over a read model that has no active generation throws a plain error that names the read model, a technical failure, and never answers an empty page (D9, E-8, Law 6) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.queryReadsActive

rule.generationRowCarries · keyed · [extension] The generation row carries the state, the projection version, the fence, the fence the last interrupt set and who started and last changed it, and nothing a batch writes on its healthy path except the state that the batch ending a pass sets; the progress row carries the cursor, the batch size and the counts, the batch size set by startGeneration and never changed after, so every pass of the generation, a resumed one and its purge included, runs at it, a purge batch capped further by limitPurgeBatch of spec:application.rebuild, and a batch writes it in the same mutation as its rows, so the progress row is the checkpoint (E-40, D9, F1) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.generationRowCarries

rule.generationSpansTenant · keyed · [extension] A generation spans every tenant of the deployment and the registry row names none; the tenant is named on every read-model row, on every context call a batch makes, and in the batch cursor, so no read or write of tenant data runs with an absent tenant as a wildcard, and no generation can be switched for one tenant alone (E-8, D11, Law 11) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.generationSpansTenant

rule.generationProgressRow · keyed · [extension] A generation whose progress row is in the pass backfill, verify or purge has at most one scheduled batch driving it, identified by the row's fence; a restore brings the rows back at their checkpoint and drops that batch with every pending scheduled function, so the generation is stranded until resumeChain bumps the fence and reschedules from the saved cursor, which the restore procedure's pending-work inventory and accepted branch drive for every such generation in building or verifying, and which the operator drives with resumeGeneration for a purge the restore stranded, because a purge belongs to a retired or aborted generation the inventory does not read (E-42, E-8, F12, D19) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.generationProgressRow

rule.registryReadNever · keyed · The registry is read, never incremented, in the command path; it is not an application-wide counter (D2, E-8) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.registryReadNever

rule.registryProgressRows · keyed · Registry and progress rows are operational data owned by the parent; they are never written by a context (D2, E-8) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.registryProgressRows

rule.commandDeclaredRead · keyed · [extension] A command whose declared read model has no generation to write fails as a technical failure, a plain error that names the read model, so a command never commits without its read model (E-8, D8, Law 6) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.commandDeclaredRead

rule.operatorGenerationRow · keyed · [extension] The operator a generation row records is the string the operator entry was given, as spec:command.actor-and-scope rules it: startedBy from startGeneration and changedBy from the last operator entry that changed the row (E-48, D19) · Base: none · Now: spec:application.generation-registry#rule.operatorGenerationRow
